title: Art & Culture
summary: Classical and folk dances, music and maestros, paintings and crafts, temple architecture, festivals and fairs, and India's UNESCO lists. SSC asks 1–2 culture questions in almost every shift. Nearly all are pairings: dance–state, artist–instrument, craft–state or festival–state. The tables below cover almost all of them.

subtopics.title: Classical Dances & Their Exponents
subtopics.concept: The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** recognises **8 classical dances**. The Ministry of Culture also lists **Chhau**, which makes 9. Each dance belongs to one home state, and exam questions test that pair first. Then they ask for a famous dancer, a special feature or the founder of an arts school.

tricks.title: Kerala has two, the rest one each
tricks.body: Kerala gives Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Every other dance has one home state: TN Bharatanatyam, AP Kuchipudi, Odisha Odissi, Manipur Manipuri, Assam Sattriya, UP Kathak.

example.q: Which state is home to two of the eight classical dances?

tricks.title: Exponent hooks
tricks.body: Birju is Kathak. Kelucharan is Odissi (Konark poses). Rukmini Devi revived Bharatanatyam (Kalakshetra). Vempati is Kuchipudi (village). Vallathol is Kerala Kalamandalam (Kathakali).

mistakes.wrong: Giving Kathak to Kerala because it is a famous dance.
mistakes.right: Kerala has Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Kathak is north Indian.
The Akademi recognises 8. The Ministry of Culture adds Chhau to make 9.

mistakes.wrong: Mixing up the two Kerala dances.
mistakes.right: Kathakali has green make-up and is a dance-drama. Mohiniyattam is a graceful solo.
Kalakshetra (1936) is Rukmini Devi's, for Bharatanatyam. Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) is Vallathol's, for Kathakali.

mistakes.wrong: Saying all Chhau styles use masks.
mistakes.right: Mayurbhanj (Odisha) uses no masks. Seraikella and Purulia use masks.

subtopics.notes:
### The nine dances at a glance
Learn each dance with its state. Then add one feature and one famous name.

| Dance | State | Signature feature | Famous names |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bharatanatyam** | Tamil Nadu | Oldest; temple *devadasi* roots; based on the *Natya Shastra* | Rukmini Devi Arundale, Padma Subrahmanyam, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mrinalini Sarabhai |
| **Kathak** | Uttar Pradesh / north | Only one linked with the **Mughal courts**; *chakkars* (spins), *tatkar* (footwork) | Pt. Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan |
| **Kathakali** | **Kerala** | Dance-drama; heavy make-up; green *pacha* for noble roles | Vallathol Narayana Menon, Kalamandalam Gopi |
| **Mohiniyattam** | Kerala | Graceful solo, the "dance of the enchantress" (Mohini) | Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Bharati Shivaji, Sunanda Nair |
| **Kuchipudi** | **Andhra Pradesh** | Named after Kuchipudi village (Krishna district); *tarangam* on a brass plate | Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja and Radha Reddy |
| **Odissi** | Odisha | *Tribhanga* posture; temple sculpture roots (Konark) | Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi |
| **Manipuri** | Manipur | Ras Lila of Radha and Krishna; soft, no ankle bells | Guru Bipin Singh, Jhaveri sisters |
| **Sattriya** | Assam | Created in the *sattras* (monasteries); recognised in **2000** | Guru Jatin Goswami, Indira P.P. Bora |
| **Chhau** | Odisha / Jharkhand / West Bengal | Semi-classical martial dance | none listed |

### Count and the Kerala confusion
The Akademi counts 8. The Ministry of Culture adds Chhau, so the total is 9.

Kerala has two dances: **Kathakali** and **Mohiniyattam**. Kathak is the north Indian court dance. Setters mix these up on purpose.

> **Rule:** Every other dance has one home state. Tamil Nadu is Bharatanatyam, Andhra Pradesh is Kuchipudi, Odisha is Odissi, Manipur is Manipuri, and Assam is Sattriya.

### Clues from make-up and movement
Make-up and movement name the dance faster than any list.

- **Kathakali:** elaborate green face (*pacha* means noble hero), codified hand language, heavy drums.
- **Mohiniyattam:** white *kasavu* costume and graceful *lasya* movement.
- **Manipuri:** circular, flowing, never sharp. The theme is the Ras Lila of Radha-Krishna.
- **Odissi:** the **tribhanga**, a three-bend stance.
- **Kathak:** spinning *chakkars* and rhythmic footwork. It has both Hindu and Mughal themes.
- **Sattriya:** the only classical dance born inside a monastery tradition. It comes from Srimanta Sankaradeva's 15th-century Bhakti movement.
- **Kuchipudi:** first a male Brahmin theatre, codified by Siddhendra Yogi. Dancers often balance on a brass plate.

> **Tip:** Read the clue first, then pick the dance. Green face means Kathakali. Three-bend means Odissi.

### Exponents and revival
- **Rukmini Devi Arundale** lifted Bharatanatyam out of its devadasi stigma. She founded **Kalakshetra** in **1936** at Chennai.
- **Vallathol Narayana Menon** founded **Kerala Kalamandalam** in **1930** to revive Kathakali.
- **Pt. Birju Maharaj** belonged to the Lucknow gharana of Kathak. Sitara Devi was its celebrated "Kathak queen".
- **Kelucharan Mohapatra** carried Odissi to the world stage.
- **Sonal Mansingh** is an Odissi dancer and a Padma Vibhushan awardee.

Kathak has three gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

### The Chhau triangle
Chhau is a semi-classical dance with masks and martial moves. It has three regional styles.

| Style | State | Masks |
|---|---|---|
| Mayurbhanj | Odisha | No masks |
| Seraikella | Jharkhand | Masks |
| Purulia | West Bengal | Masks |

Chhau entered UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in **2010**.

> **Watch:** Mayurbhanj is the maskless style. If an option says all three use masks, reject it.

Match the name to its dance.

Plate balance is Kuchipudi. Chakkars are Kathak. Lasya is Mohiniyattam.

example.q: Which body recognises 8 classical dances?
steps: The body works for music, dance and drama.
Its name begins with Sangeet Natak.
example.answer: Sangeet Natak Akademi (the Ministry of Culture adds Chhau to make 9)

revision: The Akademi recognises 8 classical dances. Adding Chhau makes 9.
Kerala: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. UP: Kathak.
Bharatanatyam is Tamil Nadu. Kuchipudi is Andhra Pradesh. Odissi is Odisha. Manipuri is Manipur. Sattriya is Assam.
Rukmini Devi started Kalakshetra in 1936. Vallathol started Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930.
Odissi has tribhanga. Kathak has chakkars. Sattriya comes from the sattras of Sankaradeva.
Chhau: Mayurbhanj has no masks. Seraikella and Purulia use masks. UNESCO listing in 2010.

subtopics.title: Folk Dances by State
subtopics.concept: Folk dances are tied to a state, a community or a season. Most questions ask you to pair a dance with its state. Others ask for a feature, such as sticks or bamboo, or the festival where it is performed.

tricks.title: North-East quick five
tricks.body: Cheraw is Mizo. Hojagiri is Tripura. Nongkrem is Khasi (Meghalaya). Wangala is Garo (Meghalaya). Bagurumba is Bodo (Assam).

example.q: Hojagiri, where women balance on an earthen pitcher, is a folk dance of which state?
steps: They balance on pots and bottles.

tricks.title: Men and women in Punjab
tricks.body: Bhangra goes with Bhaiya (men). Giddha goes with Girls (women).

mistakes.right: Yakshagana is the dance-drama of Karnataka. Kathakali is Kerala.

mistakes.wrong: Calling Chhau a purely classical dance.
mistakes.right: Chhau is semi-classical and martial, with three styles.
Jatra is folk theatre of Bengal.
Cheraw uses bamboo staves (Mizoram). Hojagiri uses balancing on pots (Tripura).

mistakes.wrong: Saying Durga Puja is an ICH dance.
mistakes.right: Durga Puja of Kolkata is a festival, listed in 2021.

subtopics.notes:
### The core table
Learn the bold names first. They are asked most often.

| State | Folk dances |
|---|---|
| Gujarat | **Garba** (UNESCO ICH 2023), **Dandiya Raas**, Tippani, Padhar |
| Rajasthan | **Ghoomar**, **Kalbelia** (ICH 2010), Chari, Kachchhi Ghodi, Gair |
| Punjab | **Bhangra** (men), **Giddha** (women), Jhumar |
| Haryana | Phag, Saang, Loor |
| Maharashtra | **Lavani**, Tamasha, Koli, Lezim, Dhangari Gaja |
| Karnataka | **Yakshagana**, **Dollu Kunitha**, Bhootha Kola |
| Kerala | **Theyyam**, Padayani, Oppana, Thiruvathirakali, Ottam Thullal |
| Tamil Nadu | **Karakattam**, Kummi, Kolattam, Oyilattam |
| Andhra / Telangana | Dhimsa, Kolattam, Burrakatha, Perini Shivatandavam (Telangana) |
| Odisha | Chhau (Mayurbhanj), Dalkhai, Ghumura, Gotipua |
| West Bengal | Chhau (Purulia), Gambhira, Jatra, Baul (music) |
| Bihar | Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Jhijhiya, Jhumar |
| Jharkhand | Chhau (Seraikela), Karma, Paika |
| Chhattisgarh | **Raut Nacha**, **Pandavani** (ballad, Teejan Bai), Gaur Maria, Karma, Panthi |
| Madhya Pradesh | Jawara, Matki, Tertali |
| Uttar Pradesh | Charkula, Nautanki, Raslila |
| Uttarakhand | Chholiya, Langvir Nritya, Barada Nati |
| Himachal Pradesh | **Nati** (Kullu Nati in Guinness Records), Jhora |
| Jammu & Kashmir | **Rouf**, Dumhal, Bhand Pather |
| Assam | **Bihu**, **Bagurumba** (Bodo), Jhumur (tea tribes) |
| Mizoram | **Cheraw** (bamboo dance) |
| Manipur | Thang Ta (martial), Lai Haraoba |
| Meghalaya | **Nongkrem** (Khasi), **Wangala** (Garo) |
| Nagaland | Chang Lo (Sua Lua), Zeliang |
| Tripura | **Hojagiri** (balancing on a pitcher) |
| Arunachal Pradesh | Bardo Chham, Ponung |
| Sikkim | Singhi Chham (snow-lion masks) |
| Goa | Fugdi, Dekhni |

### The North-East set
This set is a favourite in match-the-column questions.

- **Cheraw** is the bamboo dance of Mizoram.
- **Hojagiri** is the balancing dance of Tripura.
- **Nongkrem** is the Khasi dance of Meghalaya.
- **Wangala** is the Garo dance of Meghalaya.
- **Bagurumba** is the Bodo dance of Assam.

> **Tip:** Link the feature to the state. Bamboo is Mizoram. Balancing is Tripura. Khasi is Meghalaya.

### Feature and occasion clues
- **Garba** is a circular women's dance of Navratri, with clapping. **Dandiya Raas** uses sticks.
- **Ghoomar** is of Bhil origin. Rajasthan's royal houses adopted it. Women wear swirling ghagras.
- **Kalbelia** belongs to the snake-charmer Kalbelia community. Its moves imitate a serpent.
- **Bhangra** and **Giddha** mark the Baisakhi harvest.
- **Lavani** is fast, with dholki music. It grew inside the *tamasha* theatre of Maharashtra.
- **Yakshagana** is a night-long dance-drama of Karnataka with huge headgear.
- **Theyyam** is a Kerala ritual. Performers embody village goddesses, mostly male performers.
- **Bihu** is the spring (Rongali) dance of Assam.
- **Cheraw** dancers step between crossed bamboo staves clapped in rhythm.
- **Hojagiri** dancers are Reang women who balance on pots and bottles.
- **Nongkrem** is a Khasi thanksgiving dance.
- **Karma** is a dance of Karma-devi tree worship in the Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand belt.

> **Watch:** Yakshagana is Karnataka. Kathakali is Kerala. Setters put them side by side.

### The classical-folk border
Some forms sit near the line between classical and folk.

- **Chhau** is semi-classical and martial. It has three styles: Mayurbhanj, Seraikella and Purulia.
- **Yakshagana** is a folk dance-drama, not a classical dance.
- **Jatra** of Bengal is folk theatre, not a dance.

Setters swap these with classical names. Pin the state dance before you answer.

### Recognition to remember
- **Garba** entered UNESCO's ICH list in **2023**. It was India's newest dance element at that time.
- **Kalbelia, Chhau and Mudiyettu** all entered in **2010**.
- **Durga Puja of Kolkata** is a festival, not a dance. It entered the ICH list in **2021**.

The 2010 ICH trio: Kalbelia, Chhau, Mudiyettu.

subtopics.title: Music, Instruments & Maestros
subtopics.concept: India has two classical music systems. Hindustani music belongs to the north. Carnatic music belongs to the south. Exams ask which maestro plays which instrument, which class an instrument falls in, and who is the founder or master of each system.

tricks.title: Carnatic Trinity
tricks.body: T for Tyagaraja, M for Muthuswami Dikshitar, S for Syama Sastri. Purandara Dasa is the father, not part of the Trinity.

example.q: Who is called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music?
steps: The Trinity has three other names.

tricks.title: Instrument classes
tricks.body: Tata is strings. Sushira is air, so wind. Avanaddha is skin drums. Ghana is solid, such as bells, cymbals and ghatam.

mistakes.wrong: Naming Purandara Dasa as one of the Trinity.
mistakes.right: The Trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. Purandara Dasa is the father.

mistakes.wrong: Calling the shehnai a string instrument.
mistakes.right: The shehnai is a wind (sushira) instrument.

mistakes.wrong: Calling the santoor a wind instrument.
mistakes.right: The santoor is a string instrument struck with mallets.
Zakir Hussain plays the tabla. Sarod belongs to Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

mistakes.wrong: Naming Ravi Shankar as the first musician with the Bharat Ratna.
mistakes.right: M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998) came first. Ravi Shankar followed in 1999.

subtopics.notes:
### Two systems of classical music
| System | Region | Key points |
|---|---|---|
| **Hindustani** | North | Persian influence; ragas tied to the time of day; forms are *dhrupad* (oldest), *khayal*, *thumri*, *tappa*; musicians belong to gharanas |
| **Carnatic** | South | *Kriti* compositions; fixed compositions |

- The **Trinity of Carnatic music** is **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**. They lived in the 18th and 19th centuries in the Thiruvarur region of Tamil Nadu.
- **Purandara Dasa** is the "father" (Pitamaha) of Carnatic music. He is not part of the Trinity.
- The **Tyagaraja Aradhana** is held at **Thiruvaiyaru**.
- **Tansen**, at Akbar's court (one of the Navaratnas), is the fountainhead of Hindustani music.

> **Tip:** Pitamaha means Purandara Dasa. Trinity means Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, Syama Sastri.

### The four classes of instruments
The *Natya Shastra* sorts instruments by how they make sound.

| Class | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Tata** (string) | Strings are vibrated | sitar, veena, sarod, santoor, violin |
| **Sushira** (wind) | Air column | bansuri (flute), shehnai, nadaswaram |
| **Avanaddha** (membrane) | Stretched skin is struck | tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj, dholak |
| **Ghana** (solid) | Solid body is struck | ghatam, kanjira, manjira, jal tarang, cymbals |

The santoor is a string instrument with 100 strings struck by mallets. The ghatam is a clay pot.

> **Rule:** Shehnai is wind. Santoor is string. Tabla is a drum. Ghatam is solid.

### Maestros and their instruments
| Instrument | Maestros |
|---|---|
| **Sitar** | Pt. Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Anoushka Shankar |
| Sarod | Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan |
| **Shehnai** | Ustad Bismillah Khan |
| **Tabla** | Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha (Zakir's father), Kishan Maharaj |
| **Bansuri** | Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh |
| Santoor | Shivkumar Sharma, Rahul Sharma |
| Sarangi (bowed) | Pt. Ram Narayan, Sabri Khan |
| Violin | Lalgudi Jayaraman, L. Subramaniam (Carnatic); N. Rajam (Hindustani) |
| Mandolin | U. Srinivas |
| Mridangam | Palghat Mani Iyer, Umayalpuram Sivaraman |
| Veena (Saraswati) | E. Gayathri, S. Balachander |
| Mohan veena (slide guitar) | Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt |

**Ustad Allauddin Khan** belonged to the Maihar gharana. He taught Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan.

### Musicians with the Bharat Ratna
- **M.S. Subbulakshmi** (1998) was the **first musician** to receive it. She was a Carnatic vocalist.
- **Pt. Ravi Shankar** (1999) played the sitar.
- **Lata Mangeshkar** (2001) and **Ustad Bismillah Khan** (2001, shehnai) followed.
- **Pt. Bhimsen Joshi** was a Hindustani vocalist of the Kirana gharana.
- **Bhupen Hazarika** received it in 2019, after his death.

> **Watch:** Bharat Ratna years vary across sources for Bhimsen Joshi. Trust the order and the first-musician fact.

### Gharanas
- **Gwalior** is the oldest khayal gharana.
- **Kirana** is Bhimsen Joshi's line, through Abdul Karim Khan.
- Others: Jaipur-Atrauli, Agra, Patiala (Bade Ghulam Ali Khan) and Banaras (tabla and thumri).
- Tabla gharanas: Lucknow, Farrukhabad, Banaras, Punjab and Delhi.
- Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

### The violin and the nadaswaram
The European violin joined Carnatic music around the 18th and 19th centuries. Baluswami Dikshitar, brother of Muthuswami, gets the credit. It is now a key accompaniment.

The **nadaswaram** is a wind instrument. It leads temple processions in the south, paired with the **thavil** drum.

patterns.name: Instrument to class
patterns.howToSpot: How is the shehnai classified, or find the odd one out among wind, string and drum instruments.
steps: Tabla, mridangam are drums. Ghatam, kanjira are solid. Sitar, sarod, santoor are strings.
patterns.why: The class depends on how the sound is made.

example.q: The shehnai is classified as which type of instrument?
steps: Sound comes from a vibrating air column.

patterns.name: Maestro to instrument
patterns.howToSpot: A musician's name comes with four instrument options.

Shivkumar Sharma is santoor. Chaurasia is flute.
patterns.why: One instrument per maestro settles the question.

example.q: Ustad Zakir Hussain is a virtuoso of which instrument?
steps: He is the son of Ustad Allah Rakha.
Allah Rakha was a tabla legend.

patterns.name: Hindustani versus Carnatic
patterns.howToSpot: Father of Carnatic music, the Carnatic Trinity, Tansen's court, or a statement pair about the two systems.
steps: North is Hindustani: dhrupad, khayal, gharanas, Tansen.
South is Carnatic: kriti, Trinity, Purandara Dasa.
patterns.why: Each system has its own names and forms.

example.q: Who make up the Carnatic Trinity?
steps: All three lived in the Thiruvarur region.
example.answer: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri

patterns.name: Bharat Ratna musicians and gharanas

steps: Recall the order: M.S. Subbulakshmi 1998, Ravi Shankar 1999, then Lata Mangeshkar and Bismillah Khan 2001.
Gwalior is the oldest khayal gharana.

example.q: Who was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna?

patterns.howToSpot: Who taught Ravi Shankar, which gharana a singer belongs to, or the gharana of Bhimsen Joshi.
steps: Recall Allauddin Khan of Maihar as the teacher of Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan.
Bade Ghulam Ali Khan is Patiala.
patterns.why: Teacher-student lines link gharanas and maestros.

example.q: Bhimsen Joshi belongs to which gharana?
steps: His line goes back to Abdul Karim Khan.

Bismillah Khan: shehnai. Ravi Shankar: sitar. Zakir Hussain: tabla.

subtopics.title: Paintings, Textiles & Handicrafts
subtopics.concept: This subtopic pairs an art with a place. A folk painting belongs to a state. A craft or textile belongs to a town. The exam also asks about the miniature schools and a few famous painters. Learn each pair with one feature word.

tricks.title: Kalam, Patta, Phad
tricks.body: Kalamkari is Andhra (the pen, kalam). Pattachitra is Odisha (cloth, patta). Phad is Rajasthan (Pabuji scroll). Madhubani is Bihar (Mithila).

example.q: Kalamkari art is chiefly linked with which state?
steps: Its centres are Srikalahasti and Machilipatnam.

tricks.title: Bidri is Bidar
tricks.body: The craft carries its town's name. Bidriware comes from Bidar (Karnataka). Patola comes from Patan. Chanderi comes from Chanderi.

mistakes.wrong: Giving Warli to Bihar because it also uses wall art.
mistakes.right: Warli is Maharashtra. Bihar's wall art is Madhubani.
Pattachitra is Odisha (also West Bengal). Rajasthan has Phad.
Bidriware comes from Bidar, Karnataka.
Akbar founded it (Hamzanama). Jahangir's reign was its peak.

mistakes.wrong: Placing Pochampally ikat in Tamil Nadu.
mistakes.right: Pochampally is Telangana. Kanjeevaram silk is Tamil Nadu.

subtopics.notes:
### Folk and tribal paintings
| Painting | State | Hallmark |
|---|---|---|
| **Madhubani (Mithila)** | Bihar | Women's wall art; double-line borders; GI tag |
| **Warli** | Maharashtra | White rice-paste stick figures on mud walls |
| **Pattachitra** | Odisha (also West Bengal) | Cloth or palm-leaf scrolls; Jagannath themes |
| **Phad** | Rajasthan | Long cloth scrolls of Pabuji and Devnarayan |
| **Kalamkari** | Andhra Pradesh / Telangana | "Pen-work" on cloth: Srikalahasti (hand-drawn), Machilipatnam (block) |
| **Gond** | Madhya Pradesh | Tribal dots and dashes; Jangarh Singh Shyam |
| Pithora | Gujarat / MP | Rathwa and Bhil ritual walls |
| Kalighat | West Bengal | 19th-century Kolkata bazaar painting |
| **Tanjore** | Tamil Nadu | Gold foil and gems |
| Mysore | Karnataka | Gesso work and gold |
| **Cheriyal** | Telangana | Bright story scrolls |
| Saura | Odisha | Tribal wall art (*idital*) |
| **Thangka** | Sikkim, Ladakh, Arunachal | Buddhist cloth scrolls used in worship |
| **Pichwai** | Rajasthan (Nathdwara) | Backdrops of Srinathji (Krishna) |

> **Tip:** Kalamkari means pen-work, because *kalam* is a pen. Andhra Pradesh holds the pen.

### Miniature schools and painters
- **Mughal** painting began under **Akbar** with the *Hamzanama* workshops. It peaked under **Jahangir**, in portraits and naturalism. Akbar's atelier had Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad.
- **Rajasthani** schools include Kishangarh (the Bani Thani style), Mewar and Bundi.
- **Pahari** schools grew in the Himalayan foothills. **Kangra** is the best known, with Radha-Krishna themes. Basohli is also Pahari.
- **Company paintings** (late 18th to 19th century) were made for British patrons.
- The **Bengal School** was led by **Abanindranath Tagore**, whose *Bharat Mata* dates from 1905. E.B. Havell backed it and **Nandalal Bose** carried it on. It answered Western academic style with an Asian idiom.
- **Raja Ravi Varma** of Kerala painted in oils. He blended European realism with Indian subjects and spread them through mass lithographs.

### Crafts and textiles by place
| Craft | Place |
|---|---|
| **Bidriware** (silver inlay on blackened metal) | Bidar, Karnataka |
| Chikankari (shadow embroidery) | Lucknow, UP |
| Phulkari (flower work) | Punjab |
| Kantha (running stitch) | West Bengal |
| Bandhani / Bandhej (tie-dye) | Gujarat and Rajasthan |
| **Patola** (double ikat silk) | Patan, Gujarat |
| Pochampally ikat | Telangana |
| Kanjeevaram silk | Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu |
| Banarasi brocade | Varanasi, UP |
| Chanderi and Maheshwari | Madhya Pradesh |
| Paithani | Maharashtra |
| **Muga silk** (golden) | Assam |
| Pashmina | Jammu & Kashmir |
| Blue pottery | Jaipur, Rajasthan |
| Channapatna lacquer toys | Karnataka |
| Brass ware | Moradabad, UP |

> **Rule:** Many crafts are named after their town. Bidriware comes from Bidar. Patola comes from Patan.

### Memory hooks
- Women's wall art from Mithila is Madhubani (Bihar).
- White figures on mud is Warli.
- A Jagannath scroll is Pattachitra.
- Silver on black is Bidri.
- Tie-dye is Bandhani.
- A Nathdwara backdrop is Pichwai.

patterns.name: Painting to state
patterns.howToSpot: A folk painting such as Madhubani, Warli, Pattachitra or Phad with four states, or a match-the-column.
steps: Fix the big five: Madhubani Bihar, Warli Maharashtra, Pattachitra Odisha, Phad Rajasthan, Gond MP.
Thangka points to the Buddhist Himalaya (Ladakh or Sikkim).
patterns.why: Each painting has one home state.

example.q: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is native to which state?
steps: It is traditionally women's wall art.

patterns.name: Craft to place or GI tag
patterns.howToSpot: A craft such as Bidriware, Chikankari, Pochampally or Channapatna with a place question.
steps: Many crafts take their town's name.
Cross out places that do not fit.
patterns.why: Craft and town pairs are direct recall.

example.q: Bidriware, with silver inlay on blackened metal, comes from which place?
steps: The craft is named after a town.

patterns.name: Painting to feature or theme
patterns.howToSpot: A hallmark is described: white stick figures, Jagannath scrolls, Pabuji epic cloth, or pen-work cotton.
steps: Jagannath scrolls are Pattachitra. Pabuji cloth is Phad. Pen-work is Kalamkari. A Srinathji backdrop is Pichwai.
patterns.why: Each painting has one signature feature.

example.q: White rice-paste stick figures on mud walls identify which painting?

patterns.name: Miniature schools and painters
patterns.howToSpot: Mughal painting under which emperor, the Kangra school, Bengal School painters, or Ravi Varma's medium.
steps: Mughal: Akbar founds it, Jahangir peaks.
Bengal School: Abanindranath Tagore and Nandalal Bose. Ravi Varma: oil and lithography.
patterns.why: Each school has one or two names to recall.

example.q: The Hamzanama series of paintings was produced under which ruler?

patterns.name: Textile to place
patterns.howToSpot: A cloth or embroidery with a place question, such as Phulkari, Patola, Kantha or Muga.
steps: Phulkari is Punjab. Patola is Patan. Muga is Assam.
Kantha is West Bengal. Paithani is Maharashtra.
patterns.why: Textile names point to their home towns or states.

example.q: Muga silk, known for its golden colour, comes from which state?
steps: The state is in the North-East.

revision: Madhubani is Bihar. Warli is Maharashtra. Pattachitra is Odisha. Phad is Rajasthan. Gond is MP. Thangka is Ladakh.
Mughal: Akbar founded it (Hamzanama). Jahangir was the peak. Kangra is the Pahari gem.
Bengal School: Abanindranath Tagore (Bharat Mata, 1905) and Nandalal Bose.
Raja Ravi Varma: oil paintings and lithographs.
Bidri is Bidar. Chikankari is Lucknow. Phulkari is Punjab. Pochampally is Telangana.

subtopics.title: Temple & Rock-cut Architecture
subtopics.concept: Indian temples follow three styles: Nagara in the north, Dravida in the south and Vesara in the Deccan. Each style has its own tower and layout. The exam also asks who built a famous monument, which caves belong to which faith, and what a temple part is called.

tricks.title: Shikhara North, Gopuram South
tricks.body: A gopuram means Dravida. A curved shikhara means Nagara. A star-shaped Hoysala plan means Vesara (Deccan).

example.q: The towering gateway called a gopuram is a feature of which style?

tricks.title: Odisha pagodas
tricks.body: Black Pagoda is Konark (dark stone, Sun temple). White Pagoda is Puri (whitewashed Jagannath).

mistakes.wrong: Saying vimana is the gateway tower.
mistakes.right: The vimana is the tower above the sanctum. The gateway is the gopuram.
Hoysala temples are Vesara, in Karnataka.
Konark is Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga). Rajaraja I built Brihadeeswara.
Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.
Konark is the Black Pagoda. Puri is the White Pagoda.

subtopics.notes:
### The three temple styles
| Style | Region | Hallmarks | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nagara** | North | Curvilinear *shikhara* over the sanctum; *amalaka* on top; no boundary wall | Khajuraho (Chandela), Lingaraja (Bhubaneswar), Konark, Modhera Sun Temple |
| **Dravida** | South | Pyramidal *vimana*; huge *gopuram* gateways; enclosure wall; temple tank | Brihadeeswara (Thanjavur), Meenakshi (Madurai), Srirangam, Mahabalipuram |
| **Vesara** | Deccan (Karnataka) | Mix of Nagara and Dravida; star-shaped plans | Chalukya (Pattadakal, Badami); Hoysala (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura) |

> **Tip:** Curved shikhara means north. Gopuram means south. Star plan in Karnataka means Vesara.

### Parts of a temple
- **Shikhara:** the curving tower of the north.
- **Vimana:** the pyramidal tower above the sanctum in the south.
- **Gopuram:** the tall gateway of a southern temple.
- **Mandapa:** a pillared hall.
- **Amalaka:** the ribbed stone cap on a northern shikhara.
- **Chaitya:** a Buddhist prayer hall.
- **Vihara:** a Buddhist monastery. Karle has a chaitya. Ajanta has viharas.

> **Watch:** The gopuram is a gateway. The tower above the sanctum is the vimana.

### Monument and builder
| Monument | Builder and period |
|---|---|
| Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur | Rajaraja I, Chola (c. 1010 CE) |
| Gangaikonda Cholapuram | Rajendra I, Chola |
| **Sun Temple, Konark** | Narasimhadeva I, Eastern Ganga (13th century) |
| Sun Temple, Modhera | Bhima I, Solanki (Chaulukya) |
| Kailasa temple, Ellora | Krishna I, Rashtrakuta |
| Chennakesava, Belur | Vishnuvardhana, Hoysala (1117) |
| Hoysaleswara, Halebidu | Hoysala kings |
| Kesava, Somanathapura | Hoysala, Narasimha III's reign (1268) |
| Dilwara Jain temples, Mt Abu | Solanki period (Vimal Shah's Vimal Vasahi) |
| Meenakshi, Madurai | Nayak rulers (gopurams restored and expanded) |
| Mahabalipuram rathas, Shore Temple | Pallavas: Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), Rajasimha |

### Odisha temples
- **Konark Sun Temple** is a chariot with 24 wheels. It is called the "Black Pagoda". UNESCO listed it in 1984.
- **Jagannath Temple, Puri** was built by Anantavarman Chodaganga. It is the "White Pagoda".
- **Lingaraja** stands at Bhubaneswar.

### Rock-cut caves
| Site | State | Faith and feature |
|---|---|---|
| **Bhimbetka** | Madhya Pradesh | Prehistoric rock shelters and paintings (UNESCO 2003) |
| **Ajanta** | Maharashtra | Buddhist; 29-30 caves; murals such as Padmapani |
| **Ellora** | Maharashtra | 34 caves: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain |
| Elephanta | Maharashtra | Shaiva; Trimurti (Maheshmurti) sculpture |
| Udayagiri-Khandagiri | Odisha | Jain caves (Kharavela) |
| Barabar | Bihar | Oldest rock-cut caves (Mauryan, Ajivikas) |

Ajanta was painted in two phases, Satavahana (c. 2nd century BCE) and Vakataka (5th century CE). The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved top-down from one rock. Mahabalipuram has Pallava monolithic rathas.

### Colonial and Indo-Saracenic
- Victoria Memorial, Kolkata.
- Gateway of India, Mumbai (1924).
- Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai (UNESCO 2004, Gothic Revival).

patterns.name: Style to region or feature
patterns.howToSpot: Which style has gopurams, or a pairing of style and region.
steps: Recall: Nagara is north with a shikhara.
Dravida is south with a vimana and gopuram.
patterns.why: Each style has one tower or gate that names it.

example.q: The shikhara is the hallmark of which temple style?
steps: It is topped with an amalaka.

patterns.name: Monument to builder or dynasty
patterns.howToSpot: Who built the Sun Temple at Konark or Brihadeeswara, or a match-the-column of temples and builders.
steps: Recall six pairs: Konark, Brihadeeswara, Modhera, Kailasa, Belur, Mahabalipuram.
patterns.why: Six pairs settle most of these questions.

example.q: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under which king?
steps: It was cut top-down from a single rock.

patterns.name: Caves to period or religion
patterns.howToSpot: Ajanta versus Ellora statements, the faith mix at Ellora, or Elephanta's deity.
steps: Ellora is Buddhist, Hindu and Jain.
Elephanta is Shiva (Maheshmurti). Mahabalipuram is Pallava.
patterns.why: Each cave site has one defining fact.

example.q: Which statement about Ellora is correct?
example.answer: Its caves serve Buddhist, Hindu and Jain worship

patterns.name: Part or feature to name
patterns.howToSpot: Definitions in disguise: what is a vimana, gopuram, mandapa, chaitya, vihara or amalaka.
steps: Match: tower above the sanctum is vimana; gateway tower is gopuram; pillared hall is mandapa.
Prayer hall is chaitya; monastery is vihara.
patterns.why: The words are fixed, so recall settles it.

example.q: In south Indian temples, what is the tower above the sanctum called?
steps: The gateway tower is the gopuram.
The sanctum tower is another word.

patterns.name: Odisha temples
patterns.howToSpot: Black Pagoda or White Pagoda, or who built the Jagannath temple at Puri.
steps: Puri was built by Anantavarman Chodaganga.
patterns.why: The two pagoda names are the usual trap.

example.q: The Jagannath Temple at Puri is known as which pagoda?

revision: Nagara has a shikhara (north). Dravida has a vimana and gopuram (south). Vesara is a mix (Deccan).
Konark is Narasimhadeva I. Brihadeeswara is Rajaraja I. Modhera is Bhima I.
Kailasa at Ellora is Krishna I, Rashtrakuta, carved top-down.
Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura are Hoysala. Pattadakal is Chalukya (UNESCO 1987).
Ajanta has Buddhist murals. Chaitya is a hall. Vihara is a monastery.

subtopics.title: Festivals & Fairs
subtopics.concept: Most festival questions pair a festival with its state. Others ask about fairs, harvest seasons or India's UNESCO cultural elements. Learn each festival with one feature word. Then learn the Kumbh cities and the year ladder of UNESCO entries.

tricks.title: Hornbill closes the year
tricks.body: The Hornbill Festival runs 1-10 December. Nagaland Statehood Day is 1 December.

example.q: The Hornbill Festival is held every year in which state?
steps: The site is Kisama Heritage Village.

tricks.title: Two cattle fairs
tricks.body: Pushkar is in Rajasthan, the Pink City state, for camels. Sonepur is in Bihar, for cattle and elephants.

mistakes.right: Chhath is Bihar (and Jharkhand): sun worship at rivers.

mistakes.wrong: Adding Varanasi to the Kumbh cities.
mistakes.right: The four are Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.
Onam is Kerala. Pongal is Tamil Nadu.
Pushkar is Rajasthan (camels). Sonepur is Bihar (cattle).

mistakes.wrong: Saying Bihu is celebrated in Bihar.
mistakes.right: Bihu is Assam. Bihar has Chhath.

subtopics.notes:
### Festival and state
| Festival | State | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Onam** | Kerala | Harvest; King Mahabali; Vallam Kali (snake-boat race); pookalam |
| **Pongal** | Tamil Nadu | Mid-January harvest; four days; Jallikattu |
| Makar Sankranti / Lohri | Many / Punjab | Lohri is the night before Sankranti |
| **Baisakhi** | Punjab | April harvest; Khalsa founded (1699) |
| **Bihu** | Assam | Rongali (spring) is the famous one |
| **Durga Puja** | West Bengal | UNESCO ICH 2021 |
| **Ganesh Chaturthi** | Maharashtra | Public utsav (Tilak's mobilisation) |
| **Chhath** | Bihar / Jharkhand | Sun worship at rivers, Kartik Shukla Shashthi |
| **Hornbill** | Nagaland | 1-10 December, Kisama; "festival of festivals" |
| Sangai | Manipur | Named after the brow-antlered deer |
| Chapchar Kut | Mizoram | Spring, after jhum clearing |
| **Wangala** | Meghalaya | Garo harvest ("100 drums") |
| **Losar** | Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal | Tibetan New Year |
| **Hemis** | Ladakh | Birth of Guru Padmasambhava; masked Cham dance |
| Ugadi | Andhra, Telangana, Karnataka | New Year |
| Gudi Padwa | Maharashtra | New Year |
| **Bonalu, Bathukamma** | Telangana | Mahakali / floral festival |
| Nuakhai | Odisha | New rice |
| Thrissur Pooram | Kerala | Elephant pageant |
| Hareli | Chhattisgarh | First festival of the farming year |
| Kharchi Puja | Tripura | Fourteen deities |
| Moatsu / Sekrenyi | Nagaland | Ao / Angami festivals |
| **Sarhul** | Jharkhand | Tribal spring festival of the sal tree |

> **Tip:** Hornbill runs 1-10 December in Nagaland. December is when Nagaland's year closes.

### Fairs (melas)
- **Kumbh Mela** rotates among **Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik**. UNESCO listed it in 2017.
- **Pushkar** (Rajasthan) is a camel and livestock fair on Kartik Purnima. It is held at the only Brahma temple.
- **Sonepur Mela** (Bihar) is among Asia's largest cattle fairs. It is at the Gandak-Ganga confluence.
- **Ambubachi Mela** is at Kamakhya, Assam.
- **Rath Yatra** is at Puri.
- Suraj Kund Crafts Mela is in Haryana.
- Nauchandi is at Meerut, UP.

> **Watch:** Varanasi, Ayodhya and Mathura are decoys. They do not host the Kumbh.

### Season logic
Most festivals follow the harvest.

- Pongal falls in mid-January (Tamil Thai month).
- Baisakhi falls in mid-April, and so does Bihu.
- Onam falls in August-September (Chingam).
- Wangala falls in autumn.

The mid-January run goes Lohri, then Makar Sankranti, then Pongal, then Bihu within a day or two.

### UNESCO cultural elements of India
| Year | Element |
|---|---|
| 2001 | Kutiyattam, Sanskrit theatre (the first) |
| 2008 | Ramlila; Vedic chanting |
| 2009 | Ramman (Garhwal, festival-theatre) |
| 2010 | Chhau, Kalbelia, Mudiyettu |
| 2013 | Sankirtana of Manipur |
| 2016 | Yoga |
| 2017 | Kumbh Mela |
| 2021 | Durga Puja in Kolkata |
| 2023 | Garba of Gujarat |

> **Note:** Kutiyattam was proclaimed in 2001. It moved to the ICH list in 2008.

### Two questions that repeat
1. Which city does not host the Kumbh? The four are Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.
2. Which dance belongs to which festival? Garba with Navratri, Bhangra with Baisakhi, Bihu with Rongali Bihu, Jallikattu with Pongal, Vallam Kali with Onam.

patterns.name: Festival to state
patterns.howToSpot: A festival with four state options: Onam, Pongal, Chhath, Hornbill, Bihu and others.
steps: Onam Kerala, Pongal TN, Chhath Bihar, Hornbill Nagaland, Bihu Assam.
Durga Puja WB, Losar Ladakh, Wangala Meghalaya, Sarhul Jharkhand.
patterns.why: Each festival has one home state.

example.q: The sun-worship festival Chhath is most identified with which state?
steps: They are made at river ghats.

patterns.name: Fair to place
patterns.howToSpot: Pushkar, Sonepur, Kumbh locations, or which fair is famous for camels or cattle.
steps: Kumbh rotates: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik.
patterns.why: Each fair has one place and one animal or purpose.

example.q: The Pushkar fair, famous for camel trading, is held in which state?
steps: It is at the town of the Brahma temple.

patterns.name: Festival to season or harvest
patterns.howToSpot: Which festival falls in January or April, harvest clusters, or the order of Lohri, Sankranti and Pongal.
steps: Place Lohri first, the night before Sankranti.
Then Makar Sankranti, which is Pongal in Tamil Nadu.
patterns.why: Harvest time sets the date of most festivals.

example.q: Which festival falls immediately after Lohri in mid-January?
steps: Tamil Nadu celebrates it as Pongal.

patterns.name: UNESCO ICH elements
patterns.howToSpot: Which Indian element entered the ICH list in a given year, or matching elements to years.
steps: Match the element to its year.
patterns.why: The ladder gives every year in one string.

example.q: Which was the first Indian element on UNESCO's ICH list?

patterns.name: Kumbh city trap
patterns.howToSpot: Which city does NOT host the Kumbh Mela, or which city hosts it.
steps: List the four: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik.
Spot the decoy: Varanasi, Ayodhya or Mathura.
patterns.why: The decoy cities sound sacred, so students choose them.

example.q: Which of these does not host the Kumbh Mela: Ujjain, Nashik, Varanasi, Haridwar?

patterns.name: Festival to dance or activity
patterns.howToSpot: Which dance or event belongs to which festival.
steps: Garba goes with Navratri, Bhangra with Baisakhi.
Jallikattu goes with Pongal. Vallam Kali goes with Onam.
patterns.why: Pair the two and half the festival questions answer themselves.

example.q: Vallam Kali, the snake-boat race, goes with which festival?
steps: It happens in Kerala at harvest.

revision: Onam is Kerala (Mahabali, Vallam Kali). Pongal is Tamil Nadu (January). Baisakhi is Punjab (Khalsa 1699).
Chhath is Bihar sun worship. Hornbill is Nagaland, December. Losar is the Ladakh new year.
Kumbh cities: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik. Pushkar is a camel fair. Sonepur is a Bihar cattle fair.
UNESCO ladder: Kutiyattam 2001, Ramlila and Vedic chanting 2008, Chhau-Kalbelia-Mudiyettu 2010, Sankirtana 2013.
Then Yoga 2016, Kumbh 2017, Durga Puja 2021, Garba 2023.

subtopics.title: UNESCO Heritage & Cultural Institutions
subtopics.concept: India has 45 World Heritage Sites as of September 2026. Most are cultural. Only a few are natural, and one is mixed. Questions ask for the state and year of recent sites and for the founding year of cultural bodies. Learn each site as three facts: site, state and year.

tricks.title: WHS count ladder
tricks.body: 2021 gives 40 (Dholavira). 2023 gives 42 (Hoysala). 2024 gives 43 (Moidams). 2025 gives 44 (Maratha forts). 2026 gives 45 (Sarnath).

example.q: The Moidams of Charaideo belong to which state?
steps: The Ahom kingdom was in the North-East.

tricks.title: Three Akademis
tricks.body: Sangeet Natak comes first (1953). Sahitya and Lalit Kala come together in 1954.

mistakes.wrong: Saying India has more than one mixed site.
mistakes.right: Only Khangchendzonga is mixed.
Dholavira is in Gujarat.
Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple is in Telangana.
2021 is Ramappa and Dholavira. 2023 is Santiniketan and the Hoysala Ensembles.

mistakes.wrong: Saying Sahitya Akademi came before Sangeet Natak.
mistakes.right: Sangeet Natak is 1953. Sahitya and Lalit Kala are 1954.

subtopics.notes:
### India's World Heritage Sites
India holds **45 sites**: 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed. The mixed site is **Khangchendzonga National Park**, Sikkim (2016).

The first batch came in **1983**: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta and Ellora.

Ahmedabad became India's first heritage city in 2017. Jaipur followed in 2019.

### Recent inscriptions
| No. | Site | State | Year |
|---|---|---|---|
| 39 | Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple | Telangana | 2021 |
| 40 | Dholavira | Gujarat | 2021 |
| 41 | **Santiniketan** | West Bengal | 2023 |
| 42 | **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (Belur, Halebidu, Somnathapura) | Karnataka | 2023 |
| 43 | **Moidams of Charaideo** (Ahom mound burials) | Assam | 2024 |
| 44 | Maratha Military Landscapes (12 forts) | Maharashtra | 2025 |
| 45 | Ancient Buddhist Site of **Sarnath** | Uttar Pradesh | 2026 |

> **Tip:** Count by year. 2021 gives 40. 2023 gives 42. 2024 gives 43. 2025 gives 44. 2026 gives 45.

### Natural and mixed sites
- **Natural:** Kaziranga, Manas, Keoladeo, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Western Ghats and Great Himalayan National Park.
- **Mixed:** only Khangchendzonga.
- Everything else is cultural.

> **Rule:** Only one mixed site exists. It is Khangchendzonga.

### Intangible Cultural Heritage elements
India has 16 elements on UNESCO's ICH list.

| Year | Elements |
|---|---|
| 2008 | Koodiyattam (Sanskrit theatre, Kerala), Ramlila, Vedic chanting |
| 2009 | Ramman (religious festival, Garhwal, Uttarakhand) |
| 2010 | Mudiyettu (Kerala), Kalbelia (Rajasthan), Chhau |
| 2012 | Buddhist chanting of Ladakh |
| 2013 | Sankirtana of Manipur |
| 2014 | Brass and copper craft of the Thatheras of Jandiala Guru (Punjab) |
| 2016 | Yoga; Nowruz (multinational) |
| 2017 | Kumbh Mela |
| 2021 | Durga Puja in Kolkata |
| 2023 | Garba of Gujarat |
| 2025 | Deepavali (the 16th) |

Koodiyattam was proclaimed in 2001 and moved to the ICH list in 2008. Some lists therefore give 2001 as the first.

### Cultural institutions
| Body | Set up | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Archaeological Survey of India** | 1861 | Custodian of monuments; Alexander Cunningham was the first Director-General |
| **Sangeet Natak Akademi** | 1953 | Music, dance, drama; New Delhi |
| **Sahitya Akademi** | 1954 | Literature; awards in 24 languages |
| **Lalit Kala Akademi** | 1954 | Visual arts |
| National School of Drama | 1959 | New Delhi |
| **FTII** | 1960 | Film and Television Institute of India, Pune |
| **INTACH** | 1984 | Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage |
| **IGNCA** | 1987 | Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, New Delhi |
| Kalakshetra | 1936 | Rukmini Devi Arundale, Chennai |
| Kerala Kalamandalam | 1930 | Vallathol Narayana Menon |

The three Akademis are the national academies of the 1950s. Sangeet Natak came first, then Sahitya and Lalit Kala together.

### How the questions are built
Most World Heritage questions test one of three things.

- **The state:** Ramappa is Telangana. Dholavira is Gujarat. Santiniketan is Bengal. The Hoysalas are Karnataka. The Moidams are Assam.
- **The year:** the 2021 pair and the 2023 pair.
- **The type:** mixed is Khangchendzonga. Natural is the wildlife set.

Institution questions test the year and the art. Performing arts is 1953. Literature and fine arts are 1954. Films are 1960. Archaeology is 1861.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following classical dance–state pairs is **NOT** correctly matched?
solvedExamples.solution: **Kuchipudi** is from **Andhra Pradesh** (Kuchipudi village, Krishna district). Tamil Nadu's classical dance is Bharatanatyam. The other three pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Only Kerala has two classical dances; Tamil Nadu has just one (Bharatanatyam), so the Kuchipudi pair must be wrong.

solvedExamples.q: **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia** is renowned as a player of the —
solvedExamples.solution: **Hariprasad Chaurasia** is India's best-known **bansuri** (bamboo flute) player (Padma Vibhushan 2000). Sitar – Ravi Shankar; sarangi – Ram Narayan; tabla – Zakir Hussain.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Chaurasia's 'Call of the Valley' pairs **flute** with Shivkumar Sharma's santoor.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following is **NOT** on UNESCO's list of India's Intangible Cultural Heritage?
solvedExamples.solution: Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017) and Garba (2023) are inscribed. **Onam** is not on the list (India's festival entries are Ramman, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja and Deepavali).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Recall the 2016–2025 run: Yoga, Kumbh, Durga Puja, Garba, Deepavali — Onam is missing.

solvedExamples.q: The Ellora caves in Maharashtra contain rock-cut shrines of which religious traditions?
solvedExamples.solution: Ellora's **34 caves** (c. 6th–10th century) include 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu (including the Kailasa temple, Cave 16) and 5 Jain caves. Ajanta, by contrast, is purely Buddhist.

practice.q: **Kathakali**, the dance-drama known for its elaborate green face make-up, is a classical dance of —
practice.solution: **Kathakali** is from **Kerala**; the poet Vallathol founded Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) to revive it. Karnataka's comparable dance-drama is Yakshagana (a folk form).

practice.q: The classical dance **Kuchipudi** takes its name from a village in which state?
practice.solution: Kuchipudi village is in the **Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh**. The dance is known for *Tarangam*, performed on the rim of a brass plate.

practice.q: **Pandit Birju Maharaj** was a celebrated exponent of —
practice.solution: **Birju Maharaj** (1938–2022) of the **Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana** was the leading figure of **Kathak** and received the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra** is associated with the revival of which dance?
practice.solution: **Kelucharan Mohapatra** (1926–2004) shaped modern **Odissi**; he was the first Odia to receive the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a dance form of —
practice.solution: **Garba of Gujarat** is performed around a lamp (*garbo*) during Navratri. It became India's 15th ICH element in December 2023.

practice.q: **Cheraw**, the bamboo dance in which dancers step in and out of clapping bamboo poles, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Cheraw** is the traditional bamboo dance of **Mizoram**, often performed at Chapchar Kut. Tripura's well-known dance is Hojagiri.
practice.shortcut: NE five: **Cheraw Mizo**, Hoja Tripura, Nong Khasi, Wang Garo, Bagu Bodo.

practice.q: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the 'Trinity' of Carnatic music?
practice.solution: The Trinity is **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**. **Purandara Dasa** (16th century) is honoured as the *Pitamaha* (father) of Carnatic music.
practice.shortcut: Tea, Milk, Sugar = T, M, S — no 'P'.

practice.q: **Ustad Bismillah Khan**, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, was a maestro of the —
practice.solution: **Bismillah Khan** of Varanasi took the **shehnai** from wedding music to the concert stage and played it at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947.
practice.shortcut: Shehnai = wind instrument of Varanasi ghats = Bismillah.

practice.q: Who was the first musician to be awarded the **Bharat Ratna**?
practice.solution: Carnatic vocalist **M.S. Subbulakshmi** received the Bharat Ratna in **1998**. Ravi Shankar followed in 1999, Lata Mangeshkar in 2001 and Bhimsen Joshi in 2009.

practice.q: **Madhubani** painting, traditionally drawn by women of the Mithila region, belongs to —
practice.solution: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is from **Bihar**, marked by double-line borders and natural colours. It has a GI tag. Odisha's scroll art is Pattachitra.

practice.q: **Kalamkari**, the art of hand-painting or block-printing cotton textiles with natural dyes, is chiefly associated with —
practice.solution: Kalamkari ('pen-work') is practised at **Srikalahasti** (free-hand) and **Machilipatnam** (block-printed) in **Andhra Pradesh**.

practice.q: **Bidriware**, a metal craft with silver inlay on a blackened alloy, originated in —
practice.solution: Bidri work takes its name from **Bidar in Karnataka**, where it developed under the Bahmani sultans. Moradabad is known for brassware.
practice.shortcut: The craft carries its town's name: **Bidri** → **Bidar**.

practice.q: The **Sun Temple at Konark** was built by —
practice.solution: The Eastern Ganga king **Narasimhadeva I** built Konark in the 13th century as a giant chariot of the Sun god with 24 wheels. Anantavarman Chodaganga built the Jagannath temple at Puri; Kharavela is linked with the Hathigumpha inscription.

practice.q: Towering gateways called **gopurams** are a characteristic feature of which temple style?
practice.solution: In the **Dravida** style the sanctum is topped by a pyramidal **vimana**, and later temples have huge **gopurams** in the enclosure walls (e.g. Meenakshi temple, Madurai). Nagara temples have a curved shikhara and no gopuram.

practice.q: The **Hornbill Festival**, called the 'festival of festivals', is held every December in —
practice.solution: The Hornbill Festival is held from **1 to 10 December** at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, **Nagaland**, showcasing all Naga tribes.

practice.q: The **Sonepur Mela**, one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held at the confluence of the Gandak and the Ganga in —
practice.solution: Sonepur (Saran district, **Bihar**) hosts the fair from Kartik Purnima. Rajasthan's famous camel fair is at Pushkar.

practice.q: **Ramman**, a religious festival and ritual theatre inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2009, is performed in —
practice.solution: Ramman is performed in the Saloor-Dungra villages of **Chamoli district (Garhwal), Uttarakhand**, in honour of the local deity Bhumiyal Devta.
practice.shortcut: Ramman – Garhwal – Uttarakhand (2009, right after the 2008 first batch).

practice.q: The **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas**, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023, are located in —
practice.solution: The ensemble covers the Hoysala temples at **Belur, Halebidu and Somnathapura** in **Karnataka**. It became India's 42nd World Heritage Site.

practice.q: The classical dance **Kathakali** belongs to —
practice.solution: **Kathakali** is Kerala's story-dance; Vallathol founded Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) to revive it.

practice.q: **Mohiniyattam**, the 'dance of the enchantress', is a classical dance of —
practice.solution: **Mohiniyattam** — Kerala's graceful lasya solo; Kerala thus has two classical dances, Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

practice.q: Which classical dance is associated with the state of **Assam**?
practice.solution: **Sattriya** was created by Srimanta Sankaradeva's Vaishnava tradition and preserved in the **sattra** monasteries of Assam.

practice.q: Which of the following is a classical dance of **North-East India** other than Sattriya?
practice.solution: **Manipuri** (Manipur) is classical — themed on the **raslila**; Bihu, Cheraw and Hojagiri are folk dances.

practice.q: The dancer **Kalamandalam Gopi** is a legendary performer of —
practice.solution: **Kalamandalam Gopi** — a stellar Kathakali artiste from the Kerala Kalamandalam tradition.

practice.q: **Raja and Radha Reddy** are renowned exponents of —
practice.solution: The **Reddy duo** carried Kuchipudi to world stages and run an academy in Delhi.

practice.q: **Sonal Mansingh**, a Padma Vibhushan dancer, is associated mainly with —
practice.solution: **Sonal Mansingh** — an Odissi (and Bharatanatyam) dancer, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: The elaborate **green face make-up (pacha)** is characteristic of —
practice.solution: In Kathakali, **pacha (green)** marks noble characters; knife characters wear red, demons black.

practice.q: Balancing on a **brass plate (tarangam)** while dancing is a specialty of —
practice.solution: The **tarangam** — dancing on the rim of a brass plate, sometimes with a pot on the head — is a Kuchipudi showpiece.

practice.q: The **raslila** theme of Radha and Krishna is central to which classical dance?
practice.solution: **Manipuri** dance grew out of the Vaishnava raslila tradition of Manipur; its movements are soft and circular.

practice.q:
Match the pose/feature with the dance:
1. Chakkars (spins) — Kathak
2. Lasya grace — Mohiniyattam
3. Chauka stance — Odissi
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are correct: Kathak's spins, Mohiniyattam's lasya, and Odissi's square **chauka** stance (alongside tribhanga).

practice.q: **Kerala Kalamandalam**, founded in 1930 to revive Kathakali, was set up by —
practice.solution: Poet **Vallathol Narayana Menon** founded Kalamandalam in 1930; Rukmini Devi's Kalakshetra came six years later.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Sattriya received classical dance status in 2000.
2. Chhau is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
3. Kathak has three major gharanas — Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three hold: Sattriya was recognised classical in **2000**; Chhau entered the UNESCO ICH list in **2010**; Kathak's gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

practice.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a folk dance of —
practice.solution: **Garba** is Gujarat's Navratri circle dance; it entered the UNESCO ICH list in **2023**.

practice.q: **Bhangra** and **Giddha** are folk dances of —
practice.solution: **Bhangra** is the men's dance and **Giddha** the women's — both Punjabi, tied to the Baisakhi harvest.

practice.q: The **Hojagiri** dance, famous for balancing on pots and bottles, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Hojagiri** — performed by Reang women of Tripura with astonishing balancing feats.

practice.q: **Nongkrem**, a thanksgiving folk dance, is performed by the Khasi community of —
practice.solution: **Nongkrem** — the Khasi harvest-thanksgiving dance of Meghalaya.

practice.q:
Match the North-East dances:
1. Cheraw — Mizoram
2. Hojagiri — Tripura
3. Nongkrem — Nagaland
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Nongkrem** belongs to **Meghalaya** (Khasi), not Nagaland — Nagaland's famous festival is Hornbill.
practice.shortcut: Nongkrem is Khasi — Meghalaya, not Nagaland.

practice.q: The **Lavani** dance, performed to the beats of the dholki, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Lavani** grew inside the **tamasha** folk theatre of Maharashtra; the dholki drives its tempo.

practice.q: **Theyyam**, a ritual dance in which performers embody village deities, is practised in —
practice.solution: **Theyyam** — north Kerala's ritual art where (mostly male) performers are possessed by the goddess; not a classical dance.

practice.q: **Yakshagana**, the spectacular night-long dance-drama with huge headgear, comes from —
practice.solution: **Yakshagana** is Karnataka's folk dance-drama — the Keralite counterpart is Kathakali (a classical form).

practice.q: **Bihu**, danced during the Rongali festival in April, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Rongali (Bohag) Bihu** marks the Assamese new year and spring; the Bihu dance accompanies it.

practice.q: The **Karma** dance, worshipping the Karma tree, is common to the tribal belts of —
practice.solution: **Karma** — an adivasi dance of the Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand (and adjoining MP) belt, danced around a sal/Karma branch.

practice.q: Which of the following is **NOT** a folk dance of Rajasthan?
practice.solution: **Garba** is Gujarati; Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Chari are Rajasthani.
practice.shortcut: Garba crosses the border — it's Gujarat's.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Garba was inscribed on the UNESCO ICH list in 2023.
2. Kalbelia, Chhau and Mudiyettu were inscribed in 2010.
3. Yakshagana is recognised as a classical dance of India.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Yakshagana is a folk dance-drama** — not one of the recognised classical dances. The two ICH statements are correct.

practice.q: The **tabla** is classified as which type of instrument?
practice.solution: The tabla produces sound from a struck skin — an **avanaddha vadya**.

practice.q: Which of the following is a **wind** instrument?
practice.solution: **Nadaswaram** — the south Indian temple wind instrument, usually paired with the thavil drum.

practice.q: The **santoor**, once a Kashmiri folk instrument, is classed as —
practice.solution: The santoor has around **100 strings** struck with light mallets — a stringed instrument taken to the concert stage by Shivkumar Sharma.

practice.q: Ustad **Amjad Ali Khan** is a maestro of the —
practice.solution: **Amjad Ali Khan** — sarod; the senia-maihar lineage of his family is famous for it.

practice.q: **Pt. Shivkumar Sharma**, who took a Kashmiri folk instrument to the classical stage, played the —
practice.solution: **Shivkumar Sharma** = santoor; Hariprasad Chaurasia is the flute maestro of the same era.

practice.q: **Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt** won a Grammy (1994) for playing the —
practice.solution: His redesigned **slide guitar — the mohan veena** — won the 1994 Grammy with Ry Cooder for *A Meeting by the River*.

practice.q: Ustad **Allah Rakha**, doyen of the Punjab gharana, was a master of the —
practice.solution: **Allah Rakha** was the great tabla player — father and first teacher of **Zakir Hussain**.

practice.q: Who is called the **'Pitamaha (father) of Carnatic music'**?
practice.solution: **Purandara Dasa** systematised Carnatic teaching (sarali varisai onwards); the Trinity came after him.

practice.q: **Tansen**, one of the Navaratnas, adorned the court of —
practice.solution: **Tansen** — Akbar's court musician, the fountainhead of Hindustani music and the Miyan ki Malhar raga lore.

practice.q: Which raga-family statement is correct about **Hindustani** music?
options: Ragas are traditionally tied to times of the day
The violin is its lead instrument
practice.solution: Hindustani ragas carry time-of-day (and seasonal) associations; fixed kriti composition is the Carnatic hallmark.

practice.q: **Pt. Bhimsen Joshi**, Bharat Ratna 2008, was a vocalist of which gharana?
practice.solution: **Bhimsen Joshi** sang in the **Kirana** gharana line; the oldest khayal gharana is Gwalior.

practice.q: Which is regarded as the **oldest khayal gharana** of Hindustani music?
practice.solution: **Gwalior** gharana is the oldest of the khayal gharanas; Patiala is famous for Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

practice.q:
Arrange the musician **Bharat Ratnas** chronologically:
1. Ravi Shankar
2. M.S. Subbulakshmi
3. Lata Mangeshkar
4. Bhimsen Joshi
practice.solution: MS (1998) → Ravi Shankar (1999) → Lata + Bismillah (2001) → Bhimsen Joshi (2008).

practice.q: **Pattachitra**, scroll painting with Jagannath iconography, belongs mainly to —
practice.solution: **Pattachitra** — Odisha's cloth and palm-leaf painting tradition centred on Puri's Jagannath cult.

practice.q: **Gond** tribal painting is associated with —
practice.solution: **Gond** painting — the dot-and-line tribal art of the Gond community of central India (MP).

practice.q: **Thangka** paintings, used as devotional objects in monasteries, belong to the tradition of —
practice.solution: **Thangka** — consecrated cloth scrolls of Ladakh, Sikkim and the Tibetan Buddhist world.

practice.q: **Phad**, the painted narrative scroll of the Pabuji epic, is a tradition of —
practice.solution: **Phad** — Rajasthan's bhopa priests unroll the painted scroll while singing the Pabuji/Devnarayan epic.

practice.q: **Chikankari**, the shadow-work embroidery, is a craft of —
practice.solution: **Chikankari** — Lucknow's whitework embroidery, once associated with Mughal court dress.

practice.q: **Pochampally**, famous for ikat weave with GI status, is in —
practice.solution: **Pochampally ikat** — the Telangana village whose tie-and-dye weave carries a GI tag.

practice.q: **Channapatna**, known for lacquered wooden toys, lies in —
practice.solution: **Channapatna** (Ramanagara district, Karnataka) — 'toy town' with a GI-tagged lacquer-ware tradition.

practice.q: The name **Kalamkari** literally refers to —
practice.solution: **Kalam** = pen: the Srikalahasti style is hand-drawn with a bamboo pen; the Machilipatnam style uses block prints.

practice.q: **Pichwai** paintings, made as backdrops for the deity Srinathji, belong to —
practice.solution: **Pichwai** — Nathdwara's painted curtains/backdrops behind the idol of Srinathji (Krishna).

practice.q: Mughal painting is said to have **peaked under Jahangir**; it was **founded** under —
practice.solution: Akbar founded the imperial atelier (the *Hamzanama*); Jahangir's reign brought portraiture and naturalism to their peak. (Humayun did bring the Persian masters, but the workshop flourished under Akbar.)

practice.q: The painting ***Bharat Mata* (1905)**, icon of the Swadeshi era, was painted by —
practice.solution: **Abanindranath Tagore** — founder of the Bengal School; Nandalal Bose carried the school forward.

practice.q: **Raja Ravi Varma**, famed for realistic depictions of Indian subjects, worked mainly in —
practice.solution: The Kerala painter fused European academic realism with Indian themes; his press made his gods and heroines mass-market lithographs.

practice.q: Towering **gopurams** are a characteristic feature of which temple architecture?
practice.solution: **Gopurams** — the colossal gateway towers of south Indian (Dravida) temples, e.g. Meenakshi, Srirangam.

practice.q: **Vesara**, the hybrid temple style mixing Nagara and Dravida elements, flourished under —
practice.solution: **Vesara** — the Deccan style of the Chalukyas (Pattadakal, Badami) perfected by the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu).

practice.q: The **Lingaraja temple** at Bhubaneswar follows which style?
practice.solution: Odisha's temples (Lingaraja, Konark, Jagannath Puri) follow the **Kalinga** — an eastern branch of the Nagara style with deul towers.

practice.q: The **Brihadeeswara temple** at Thanjavur was built by —
practice.solution: **Rajaraja I** raised the Chola's Rajrajeswara temple around 1010 CE; his son Rajendra I built Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

practice.q: The **Chennakesava temple at Belur** was commissioned by the Hoysala king —
practice.solution: **Vishnuvardhana** built Belur's Chennakesava (c. 1117); Halebidu and Somanathapura complete the Hoysala trio.

practice.q: The **Sun Temple at Modhera** (Gujarat) was built by —
options: Bhima I of the Solanki dynasty
practice.solution: **Bhima I** (Chaulukya-Solanki) built Modhera; the Konark Sun Temple belongs to Narasimhadeva I — don't swap the two sun temples.

practice.q: The **Dilwara Jain temples** at Mount Abu were built during the reign of the —
practice.solution: The marble Jain temples — Vimal Vasahi built by minister Vimal Shah under **Bhima I's Solanki rule**.

practice.q: The **Ajanta caves**, famous for frescoes like the Bodhisattva Padmapani, are devoted to —
practice.solution: **Ajanta** — purely Buddhist, in two phases (Satavahana, then Vakataka 5th century); painting is its glory.

practice.q: **Elephanta caves**, with the great Maheshmurti of Shiva, lie near —
practice.solution: **Elephanta** — the island caves in Mumbai harbour; a mid-first-millennium rock-cut Shiva complex (UNESCO 1987).

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Ellora's Kailasa temple was carved top-down from one rock.
2. Ajanta's caves were made in two distinct phases.
3. Ellora has only Buddhist caves.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Ellora includes **Hindu, Buddhist and Jain** caves — statement 3 fails. The top-down Kailasa cut and Ajanta's Satavahana + Vakataka phases are correct.
practice.shortcut: Ellora is three-religion — 3 is the false one.

practice.q: In Buddhist architecture, the **chaitya** was the —
practice.solution: **Chaitya** = congregational prayer hall (apse-ended, pillared); **vihara** = the monks' monastery.

practice.q: The ribbed stone **amalaka** crowns the shikhara of which temples?
practice.solution: The **amalaka** — a ribbed, myrobalan-shaped cap topped by a kalasha — sits on the northern shikhara.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Konark — Narasimhadeva I
2. Gangaikonda Cholapuram — Rajendra I
3. Meenakshi gopurams — Nayak rulers
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three correct: Konark (Eastern Ganga), the Chola's second capital temple (Rajendra I), and Madurai's towering gopurams rebuilt by the Nayaks.

practice.q: **Onam**, celebrating King Mahabali's annual homecoming, is the harvest festival of —
practice.solution: **Onam** — Kerala's Chingam-month festival with pookalam flower carpets and the Vallam Kali snake-boat races.

practice.q: The **Hornbill Festival**, the 'festival of festivals', is held every December in —
practice.solution: **Hornbill** — 1–10 December at Kisama near Kohima, showcasing all Nagaland tribes.

practice.q: **Losar**, the new-year festival, is celebrated mainly in —
practice.solution: **Losar** — the Tibetan Buddhist new year of the trans-Himalayan belt.

practice.q: **Sarhul**, the spring festival worshipping the sal tree, belongs to the tribal culture of —
practice.solution: **Sarhul** — Jharkhand's adivasi spring festival centred on the sal tree and nature worship.

practice.q: **Wangala**, the hundred-drum harvest festival, is celebrated by the **Garo** community of —
practice.solution: **Wangala** — the Garos of Meghalaya thank the sun god Misi Sal after harvest.

practice.q: The **Kumbh Mela** does NOT rotate through which city?
practice.solution: The four Kumbh venues: **Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik** — Varanasi is not one.

practice.q: The **Sonepur fair**, one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held in —
practice.solution: **Sonepur** (near Patna) — at the Gandak-Ganga confluence; Pushkar in Rajasthan is the camel fair, Sonepur the elephant-cattle fair.

practice.q: **Jallikattu**, the bull-embracing sport, is associated with which festival?
practice.solution: **Jallikattu** — Tamil Nadu's bull sport during the Pongal season (Mattu Pongal).

practice.q:
Arrange by calendar:
1. Baisakhi
2. Pongal
3. Onam
4. Rongali Bihu
Which order is correct?
practice.solution: Pongal (mid-Jan) → Baisakhi (mid-Apr) → Rongali Bihu (mid-Apr, days after Baisakhi) → Onam (Aug–Sep).

practice.q: **Durga Puja** of Kolkata entered the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in —
practice.solution: **Durga Puja in Kolkata** — inscribed in **2021**; Garba followed in 2023.

practice.q: **Ramman**, the ritual festival-theatre of Garhwal on the UNESCO ICH list, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Ramman** — the Salur-dun village ritual of Garhwal, **Uttarakhand**, inscribed in **2009**.

practice.q:
Match the ICH inscriptions:
1. Yoga — 2016
2. Kumbh Mela — 2017
3. Sankirtana — Manipur, 2013
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are right: Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), and Manipur's **Sankirtana** (2013).

practice.q: **Dholavira**, the Harappan city inscribed as a UNESCO WHS in 2021, is in —
practice.solution: **Dholavira** (Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat) — 2021's second Indian inscription with Ramappa.

practice.q: **Santiniketan**, Rabindranath Tagore's university town, was inscribed as a UNESCO WHS in —
practice.solution: **Santiniketan** (West Bengal) — inscribed in **2023**, the same year as the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.

practice.q: The **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura) are located in —
practice.solution: The Hoysala temples — Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura — all in **Karnataka**, inscribed in 2023.

practice.q:
Arrange the recent Indian WHS inscriptions:
1. Santiniketan
2. Ramappa temple
3. Moidams of Assam
4. Dholavira
practice.solution: Ramappa + Dholavira (2021) → Santiniketan (2023) → Moidams (2024).

practice.q: The **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India's national academy of performing arts, was set up in —
practice.solution: **SNA 1953** — a year before the Sahitya (1954) and Lalit Kala (1954) Akademis.

practice.q: The **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)** is located at —
practice.solution: **FTII (1960)** — on the former Prabhat Studio campus in Pune.

practice.q: Which Akademi is concerned with **fine arts (painting, sculpture, graphics)**?
practice.solution: **Lalit Kala Akademi (1954)** = visual arts; Sahitya = literature; Sangeet Natak = music-dance-drama.

practice.q: Which of the following is a **natural** World Heritage Site of India?
practice.solution: **Kaziranga** (Assam, 1985) — with Manas, Keoladeo and Sundarbans in the natural list.

practice.q: **Keoladeo National Park**, a natural WHS famous for birds, is in —
practice.solution: **Keoladeo (Bharatpur), Rajasthan** — inscribed 1985; the Sundarbans bird-adjacent natural site is in Bengal.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Khangchendzonga National Park is India's only mixed WHS.
2. The Western Ghats are a natural WHS.
3. Manas National Park is a cultural WHS.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Manas is natural**, not cultural — Assam's pair (Kaziranga, Manas) is both natural.

practice.q: India's **first four** World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1983, included —
options: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora
practice.solution: The 1983 batch: **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora**; Konark and Mahabalipuram followed in 1984.

practice.q: The **Archaeological Survey of India's** first Director-General was —
practice.solution: **Alexander Cunningham** — the 'father of Indian archaeology', first DG from 1861.

practice.q:
Match the inscriptions:
1. Ramappa temple — Telangana, 2021
2. Maratha Military Landscapes — 2025
3. Sarnath Buddhist site — 2026
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three: Ramappa (Telangana, 2021), the Maratha fort landscapes of Maharashtra-Tamil Nadu (2025), and Sarnath (2026) — India's most recent inscriptions.
